Of the 10% allocation to load, 7% was allocated to SPP and 3% to MISO-based production cost modeling to estimate the benefit to each region. After the projects received $464.5 million in grants through the Department of Energy’s Grid Resilience and Innovation Partnership program, the cost allocation was updated to 100% of the remaining engineering and construction costs would be paid for by interconnection generators (MISO Planning Advisory Committee 2023). These costs would be spread over generator interconnection projects across multiple queue clusters to reduce the impact on any single interconnecting customer (SPP and MISO 2023). Electricity load between MISO and SPP would continue to pay for operations and maintenance costs and would serve as a backstop for undersubscribed capacity. In November 2024, FERC approved the JTIQ cost allocation proposal (FERC 2024c). The JTIQ transmission projects do not provide reliability or economic benefits as defined in the MISO or SPP tariffs and would not have been identified as transmission solutions in either region’s transmission planning process (FERC 2024c). The joint planning and cost allocation approach taken by MISO and SPP helped identify projects that support generator interconnection and provide regional benefits that may not have otherwise been built. 62 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies at www.nlr.gov/publications.
